h1: 12 Things to Do in Machu Picchu (2026)
intro: Machu Picchu is more than a single viewpoint. From sunrise at the citadel to hiking Huayna Picchu, soaking in Aguas Calientes hot springs, and exploring the Site Museum — here is what to prioritize on your visit, with tips from our team in Cusco.

sections.heading: What to visit in Machu Picchu? | The Essential Stops
sections.body: You might ask, “What are the must-see spots inside the citadel?” The site is vast, but certain areas are non-negotiable for understanding its grandeur. The Temple of the Sun A masterpiece of precision. The Architecture: It is the only curved building in the citadel. The stones are polished to perfection. The Mystery: On the winter solstice, the sun shines directly through its window, illuminating the ceremonial rock inside. Temple of the Sun in Machu Picchu – Perú Grand Travel The Intihuatana The “Hitching Post of the Sun.” The Energy: Legend says that if you place your hands near it (without touching!), you can feel the energy of the earth. It was used to predict solstices. The Temple of the Condor A stunning example of organic architecture. The Design: The Incas used a natural rock formation on the ground to shape the head and neck of a condor, adding stone wings above. It represents the spirit world. For a deeper dive into these structures, read our guide on Museums in Machu Picchu to understand the artifacts found here. DID YOU KNOW? No Roofs: You will notice the buildings have no roofs. The Incas used ichu grass (straw) tied to wooden beams. Over centuries, the organic material disintegrated, leaving only the stone skeletons.

sections.heading: Where to take the best photos in Machu Picchu?
sections.body: We live in a visual world. If you want that shot, you need to know where to stand. The Guardian’s House: This is the classic postcard spot. It offers the full panoramic view of the citadel with Huayna Picchu in the background. Go early in the morning for the best light. The Sun Gate | Inti Punku: For a wide-angle shot that captures the isolation of the city in the mountains. The Llama Selfie: Llamas roam freely on the agricultural terraces. sections.heading: What are the top 10 things to do in Machu Picchu Pueblo?
sections.body: Often called Aguas Calientes, the town at the base of the mountain is more than just a transit hub. There are several things to do in Machu Picchu Pueblo that deserve your attention before or after your visit to the ruins. Soak in the Thermal Springs: Give your legs a rest in the natural volcanic waters that give the town its name. Visit the Butterfly House | Mariposario: A lovely conservation project featuring local species. Explore the Artisan Market: Find high-quality alpaca knits and silver jewelry. Dine at Luxury Restaurants: Try the gourmet fusion at Indio Feliz or Tree House . Walk the Mandor Gardens: A lush botanical garden with a private waterfall. Visit the Museo de Sitio Manuel Chávez Ballón: One of the essential museums in Machu Picchu located near the Puente Ruinas. Enjoy a Pisco Sour by the River: The sound of the Urubamba is the perfect soundtrack for a sunset drink. Hike to Putucusi Mountain: For a challenging, vertical climb with a unique side view of the ruins. Stroll through the Sculpture Plaza: Admire the large stone carvings that tell Incan legends. Taste local craft beer: Many small breweries are popping up in the pueblo.

sections.heading: Things to do in Machu Picchu Pueblo | Aguas Calientes
sections.body: The adventure doesn’t end at the exit gate. The town below, Aguas Calientes, has its own charm. The Hot Springs The town is named after them! The Experience: Soak in the natural thermal baths nestled in the canyon. It is rustic but relaxing after a hike. The Artisan Market Located next to the train station. The Shopping: It is a labyrinth of alpaca sweaters, silver jewelry, and art. It is the perfect place to buy gifts before boarding your train. The Mandor Gardens A short walk from town along the train tracks. The Nature: A private reserve with a waterfall and botanical gardens. It is a quiet escape from the crowds. For hotel recommendations in town, check our guide on Luxury Hotels in Aguas Calientes . Hot springs Machu Picchu – Perú Grand Travel

sections.heading: What to do in Machu Picchu at night?
sections.body: Unlike Cusco, Machu Picchu Pueblo is quiet at night. But there is magic in the silence of the canyon. Dinner by the River Many restaurants have terraces overlooking the rushing Urubamba River. The sound of the water is the perfect soundtrack for a dinner of trout or alpaca. Recommendation: Try the Indio Feliz for a fusion of French and Peruvian cuisine in a quirky, garden setting. .ctaText { font-weight:bold; color:#464646; text-decoration:none; font-size: 16px; } .postTitle { color:#000000; text-decoration: underline!important; font-size: 16px; } .postTitle { text-decoration: underline!important; }

sections.heading: What are the must-eat local dishes and where?
sections.body: Food is a vital part of the things to do in Machu Picchu . In the pueblo, you are spoiled for choice. Pachamanca: A traditional meal cooked in an earth oven—a true Andean ritual. Alpaca Steak: Surprisingly lean and delicious, often served with a chimichurri sauce. Quinoa Soup: The “golden grain” of the Incas is the perfect warm-up for a chilly mountain evening. For a high-end experience, the restaurants at the Belmond Sanctuary Lodge (right at the entrance) allow you to dine with a view that no other place on earth can match. This is a highlight among the many things to do in Peru 2026 .
